title: Validate dimension name lengths
description: Both should be `length(colnames) != length(widths)` (resp. rownames/heights). As written, `length(colnames == length(widths))` equals `length(colnames)`, which is truthy for any non-NULL non-empty value. The length-mismatch validation never fires (and empty-but-non-NULL input slips through).

title: Add "Supported By Posit" badge to gtable website
description:
## Overview

This PR adds the "Supported by Posit" badge to the gtable website.

## Background

We've recently started adding a "Supported by Posit" badge across all Posit package websites to create a more cohesive brand presence. The badge appears on the far right of the top navigation bar or at the bottom of the hamburger menu. It links to Posit’s main website. @hadley is involved with this initiative.

The following websites already have the "Supported by Posit" badge: [ggplot2](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org), [Great Tables](https://posit-dev.github.io/great-tables/articles/intro.html), [gt](https://gt.rstudio.com), [Plotnine](https://plotnine.org), [Pointblank](https://posit-dev.github.io/pointblank/), [pointblank](https://rstudio.github.io/pointblank/), and [Quarto](https://quarto.org).

See https://posit-dev.github.io/supported-by-posit/ for more information.

## Changes

- Added a line to `_pkgdown.yml` to include the JavaScript file
- Standardized indentation in `_pkgdown.yml`

title: Avoid partial match of `just` to `justification`
description:
This PR aims to fix https://github.com/tidyverse/ggplot2/issues/5654.

Briefly, when a viewport is provided to `gtable()`, it is reconstituted but the `justification` field is extracted via `$just`.
This PR changes this to `$justification`, avoiding the partial match.

The reprex from https://github.com/tidyverse/ggplot2/issues/5654#issuecomment-1902198119 now does not throw an error:

``` r
devtools::load_all("~/packages/gtable/")
#> ℹ Loading gtable
library(grid)
options(warnPartialMatchDollar = TRUE)
options(warn = 2) 

gtable(
  widths = unit(1, "cm"),
  heights = unit(1, "cm"),
  vp = viewport()
)
#> TableGrob (1 x 1) "layout": 0 grobs
```

<sup>Created on 2024-01-23 with [reprex v2.1.0](https://reprex.tidyverse.org)</sup>

gtable_trim now works with empty tables
description:
Fix #37 

Before, calling `gtable_trim()` on an empty gtable object would result in an incomprehensible error message: 

```r
Error in seq.int(w[1], w[2]) : 'from' must be a finite number
In addition: Warning messages:
1: In min(x) : no non-missing arguments to min; returning Inf
2: In max(x) : no non-missing arguments to max; returning -Inf
3: In min(x) : no non-missing arguments to min; returning Inf
4: In max(x) : no non-missing arguments to max; returning -Inf
```

This had further repercussions for `gtable_filter()` that called `gtable_trim()` by default and might return an empty gtable

title: Finer control of gtable_show_layout
description: In the current implementation, `gtable_show_layout()` uses default parameter settings of `grid::grid.show.layout()`. One can call `grid.show.layout()` directly, but since `gtable_layout()` is not exported, the user would first have to construct the layout object "by hand". The proposed change offers a small convenience in being able to adjust display parameters (such as `vp.ex`) directly through `gtable_show_layout()`.

title: Assembly improvements
description:
This PR includes a range of improvements related to performance of gtable assembly. The main points are:

- Faster `data.frame` construction using the `new_data_frame()` constructor
- Avoiding `rbind`'ing layout data frames together
- Fast data.frame indexing and modifications by either using `.subset2()` or treating the layout data frame as a list internally
- Avoid calls to `nrow(x)`/`ncol(x)` in favour of length(x$heights)/length(x$widths)
- Substitute `stopifnot(...)` with `if (...) stop()` expressions

title: absolute.size not needed in width/heightDetails
description:
cf email discussion with Paul Murrell, Hadley and Winston (23/07/2015):
no-one seems to remember why `absolute.units` was used here in the first
place. But it is rather inconvenient in practice -- consider this one example for illustration:

```
absolute.size(unit.c(unit(1,"npc"), 
                      unit(1,"grobwidth", data=textGrob("label"))))
[1] 1null 1null
```

Not what’s usually intended, and problematic if one wants a tight layout based on the string width.

title: unit comparison with arithmetic units
description:
`compare.unit` fails with arithmetic units:

``` r
s1 <- max(grobWidth(textGrob("a")), grobWidth(textGrob("1")))
s2 <- max(grobWidth(textGrob("a")), grobWidth(textGrob("2")))
gtable:::compare.unit(s1, s2, pmin)
unit.pmin(s1, s2)
```

Better use `unit.pmax` and `unit.pmin` I think.

title: Fixes to print order
description:
`print.gtable`: print z order but don't sort names by z order

Previously, the layout names were sorted by z order, but the grobs weren't. This resulted in a mismatch between the names and the grobs. It's better to not sort by z by default, since that doesn't match how indexing works. The new `zsort` option allows the output to be sorted by z.

Old output:

```
p <- qplot(1:3, 1:3, colour=1:3)
g <- ggplotGrob(p)

# Print out the table
# Note there's a bug in the ordering of the names. They're sorted by the
# z order, but they shouldn't be. This is fixed in the devel version of
# gtable.
g
# TableGrob (6 x 6) "layout": 9 grobs
#   (1-6,1-6) background: rect[plot.background.rect.105]
#   (4-4,3-3) spacer: absoluteGrob[GRID.absoluteGrob.89]
#   (3-3,4-4) panel: zeroGrob[NULL]
#   (3-3,3-3) axis-l: gTree[GRID.gTree.77]
#   (4-4,4-4) axis-b: absoluteGrob[GRID.absoluteGrob.83]
#   (5-5,4-4) xlab: text[axis.title.x.text.91]
#   (3-3,2-2) ylab: text[axis.title.y.text.93]
#   (3-3,5-5) guide-box: gtable[guide-box]
#   (2-2,4-4) title: text[plot.title.text.103] 
```

New output:

```
g
# TableGrob (6 x 6) "layout": 9 grobs
#   z     cells       name                               grob
#1 0 (1-6,1-6) background      rect[plot.background.rect.44]
#2 3 (3-3,3-3)     axis-l absoluteGrob[GRID.absoluteGrob.28]
#3 1 (4-4,3-3)     spacer                     zeroGrob[NULL]
#4 2 (3-3,4-4)      panel               gTree[GRID.gTree.16]
#5 4 (4-4,4-4)     axis-b absoluteGrob[GRID.absoluteGrob.22]
#6 5 (5-5,4-4)       xlab         text[axis.title.x.text.30]
#7 6 (3-3,2-2)       ylab         text[axis.title.y.text.32]
#8 7 (3-3,5-5)  guide-box                  gtable[guide-box]
#9 8 (2-2,4-4)      title           text[plot.title.text.42]

print(g, zsort=TRUE)
# TableGrob (6 x 6) "layout": 9 grobs
#   z     cells       name                               grob
#1 0 (1-6,1-6) background      rect[plot.background.rect.44]
#3 1 (4-4,3-3)     spacer                     zeroGrob[NULL]
#4 2 (3-3,4-4)      panel               gTree[GRID.gTree.16]
#2 3 (3-3,3-3)     axis-l absoluteGrob[GRID.absoluteGrob.28]
#5 4 (4-4,4-4)     axis-b absoluteGrob[GRID.absoluteGrob.22]
#6 5 (5-5,4-4)       xlab         text[axis.title.x.text.30]
#7 6 (3-3,2-2)       ylab         text[axis.title.y.text.32]
#8 7 (3-3,5-5)  guide-box                  gtable[guide-box]
#9 8 (2-2,4-4)      title           text[plot.title.text.42]
```

I'm not sure I got the documentation right, since there's a new parameter with an S3 method.

title: Rewrite gtable rendering code.
description:
This makes it handle nested gtables better. It is also much simpler than the previous version. @kohske I think this addresses your comments in #26.

Instead of using `childrenvp` in a `gTree`, it sets the `vp` for each grob. Also, it doesn't set any `vp` arguments to `vpPath` objects (these aren't `viewport` objects, and this caused problems before). Now it uses `vpStack` objects instead.

Some test output is here: http://rpubs.com/wch/931

title: Turn gtable into a grob
description:
This is my initial attempt to turn the gtable into a grob, based on @baptiste's code.

This code uses `grid.draw()` to draw the gtable as a grob:

```
a <- gtable(unit(1:3, c("cm")), unit(5, "cm"))
a
gtable_show_layout(a)

# Add a grob:
rect <- rectGrob(gp = gpar(fill = "black"))
a <- gtable_add_grob(a, rect, 1, 1)
a <- gtable_add_grob(a, rect, 1, 3)
a

# Draw using grid
grid.newpage()
grid.draw(a)

# Can still use plot()
plot(a)
```

Input is appreciated!

@kohske, I mentioned in the other branch that I thought it was better to continue on that branch -- but here I am making a new branch. Sorry for the confusion...
